judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied Process Explorer evidence and confirmed File Explorer add-ons are enabled. Current Run image loading calls Windows shell item/image APIs and associated-icon extraction inside PowerLauncher, a known in-process extension loading boundary.
evidence: Process Explorer screenshots show shell-extension modules loaded in PowerToys.PowerLauncher.exe.
The reporter develops shell extensions and must stop PowerToys to update them.
Wox.Infrastructure.Image.WindowsThumbnailProvider creates IShellItem image factories and extracts associated icons in the launcher process.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with a test shell extension and design isolation or icon-loading restrictions that prevent arbitrary shell handlers from loading into PowerLauncher.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix exists; current in-process shell image APIs provide a focused likely cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate shell icon and thumbnail extraction from PowerLauncher
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PowerToys Run resolves result imagery through shell COM and associated-icon APIs inside the launcher process, allowing registered third-party shell handlers to load into PowerLauncher and hold their DLLs.
plan: Identify which ImageLoader paths request IconOnly, ThumbnailOnly, or associated icons for Program/File Explorer results.
Move handler-invoking extraction to a short-lived broker process or use a shell API/flag that avoids loading third-party thumbnail/preview handlers for icon-only results.
Cache only serialized bitmap output in PowerLauncher and release the broker after extraction.
verification: Register a diagnostic shell extension and verify Process Explorer no longer shows its DLL in PowerToys.PowerLauncher.exe.
Verify icons and optional thumbnails still render for executables, links, folders, documents, and UWP apps.
Test extension update/uninstall while PowerToys Run remains active.

confidence.rationale: The in-process shell image path is confirmed, but a controlled extension trace is needed to identify which API loads the reported DLL and the least disruptive isolation boundary.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run can load third-party shell-extension DLLs while resolving result icons or thumbnails, which locks those binaries and interferes with extension deployment.
known_information: PowerToys 0.61.1 was affected and Process Explorer screenshots were supplied.
The reporter confirms File Explorer extensions are enabled and is actively deploying shell extensions.
Current launcher image code uses IShellItemImageFactory and ExtractAssociatedIcon.
inferences: A shell image request, rather than the File Explorer add-on module itself, is likely causing DLL activation inside PowerLauncher.
issue_context.analysis: The impact is a real process-lifetime lock on third-party binaries. A controlled provider test can pinpoint the API before selecting broker versus flag-based mitigation.

Process Explorer or equivalent module tracing
steps: Start PowerToys Run and clear its image cache.
Query an item associated with the diagnostic shell extension.
Record when the extension DLL enters PowerToys.PowerLauncher.exe and which result/image path triggered it.
Disable generated thumbnails and repeat to distinguish icon-only from thumbnail loading.
